_doc: Phase 5 learning-from-corrections follow-up set for the TENTH held-out project (cJSON v1.7.19, samples/realworld/cJSON). Two kinds of case. PARAPHRASE (field 'paraphrase_of' = main id, ids end in -p): every behavioural question of bench/realworld_heldout10.json reworded, asking for exactly the same answer with the same must_mention; it measures whether a correction taught on the main question carries over to new wording. NEIGHBOUR (field 'neighbour_of' = main id, ids end in -n): a different question in the same area of the code whose correct answer is a DIFFERENT place (its own must_mention, grepped verbatim in the source and checked to be where the behaviour is decided); it measures that a learned correction does not over-generalise and pull nearby questions to the corrected answer. Written from the source alone, together with the main suite, BEFORE any Verity run.

cases.q: If the JSON text is a thousand opening square brackets in a row, does the parser keep descending, or does it stop at some depth?
What happens when I make a deep copy of a tree that is nested extremely deeply, or that loops back on itself?
Where and why does parsing fail when a lone '-' appears where a number is expected?
What gets written out when a number value that holds NaN or infinity is printed?
How does the parser deal with input like {"key": "abc where the string's closing double quote is missing?
How is an invalid UTF-16 surrogate pair inside a string handled, for example \uD83D followed by \u0041?
What does the printer write when a string value contains a control byte such as 0x01?
If allocating a node fails partway through parsing the key/value pairs of an object, what happens to the members that were already parsed?
When printing into a fixed-size buffer supplied by the caller that is too short, does the library try to grow it, and what does the print call report?
If I parse with the option that rejects anything after the JSON value, what happens to input like {"a":1} xyz?
What happens when the input text begins with a UTF-8 byte order mark?
Is the ordinary object member lookup case-sensitive? Would looking up "ID" match a member called "id"?
With the normal JSON Pointer lookup, does a pointer such as /Name match an object member that is stored as "name"?
Is a JSON Pointer such as /items/007 accepted when /items is an array?
When applying a list of JSON Patch operations, what happens if one of them has an op name that is not add, remove, replace, move, copy or test?
What happens when a JSON Patch add operation targets an array index past the end of the array, for example index 10 in a 3-element array?
